default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-208.title: Wick-ceiling closing-high fade
E-208.hypothesis: A new N-minute closing high that still sits below the window's intrabar high means closes are climbing back into a zone where sellers already rejected prices with a wick; those sellers' resting offers are still above and the buyers chasing the closing high meet them, so fade the closing-basis break (mirror for lows).

E-209.title: Post-narrow-session break follow
E-209.hypothesis: Crabel's narrow-range idea across sessions: after a session whose range was well below the 20-session average, volatility is compressed and range expansion is due; day traders sized for a quiet day keep tight stops just beyond short-term extremes, so today's breaks of the recent high/low extend; follow them only on the day after a narrow session.

E-210.title: Mid-range micro-break fade
E-210.hypothesis: On a day with a normal-or-wide range, a break of the last few minutes' high/low that happens in the middle of the session range is not at any level anyone watches: no stops or breakout orders sit there, only a small push through quotes that liquidity providers lean back on; fade breaks made mid-range.

E-211.title: Seasonal reversal-regime micro-break fade
E-211.hypothesis: Some times of day are dominated by liquidity provision (bar returns reverse), others by order-flow continuation; the lag-1 autocorrelation of bar returns at this minute over the last 20 sessions measures which; where it is negative, a close beyond the recent high/low is quote bouncing that market makers reverse, so fade it only in the reversal-prone times of day.

E-212.title: Overhead-supply break-even fade
E-212.hypothesis: When a large share of the last hours' volume traded above the current price, many of those buyers are under water; a rally to a new 15-minute high brings price back toward their cost and they sell to get out at break-even, capping the push; fade the break into heavy overhead volume (mirror: trapped shorts below).

E-213.title: Developing daily-candle tail bias
E-213.hypothesis: After the first hour, a session whose high stands far above both its open and the current price is drawing a long upper tail on every daily chart: higher prices were tried and rejected, and day traders read the day as bearish; the first bar closing below the previous low joins that rejection (mirror for a long lower tail).

E-214.title: Renko reversal after a brick run
E-214.hypothesis: Renko charts are widely used by WIN day traders; bricks sized from the typical daily range turn colour only after a two-brick move against the run. After a run of several bricks the run's holders exit on the first reversal brick and Renko users reverse at the same time, so follow the reversal brick.

E-215.title: Two-sided-session micro-break fade
E-215.hypothesis: When, after the opening half hour, the session has extended both its high and its low within the recent window, both stop pools were swept and the day is rotating around value with responsive traders on both sides; a short-term break that does not reach a new session extreme is then reabsorbed, so fade it.

E-216.title: Calming-tape momentum follow
E-216.hypothesis: Volatility-managed momentum: a move larger than usual for its horizon made while bar-to-bar volatility is falling is orderly, persistent flow (a parent order being worked), not a forced burst that reverts; follow the move at the bar it becomes large while the tape is calming.

E-217.title: Open-drive day pullback resumption
E-217.hypothesis: A session whose open is still near its low an hour or more in (and price above VWAP) is an open-drive day: initiative buyers lifted from the first trade and nobody could push below the open. A short pullback of one to three lower closes is profit-taking, and the first close above the previous high is the drive resuming; follow it (mirror for an open near the high).
